//: What the DESKTOP and MOBILE release train produces, declared. Before this file existed the
fork had no statement of what it BUILDS -- only two workflows, which answer 'what did we find
a job for' and cannot answer 'what are we failing to build'. A list is not a matrix, and the
difference is invisible in a report: both read as rigour.
packaging/platforms.test.mjs holds the workflows to this file, in both directions.
A DECLARATION NOTHING ENFORCES IS A SECOND DOCUMENT TO GO STALE.
THREE CHANNELS, BECAUSE TWO COLLAPSE A POLICY INTO AN ACCIDENT. `channel` is where an asset
goes WHEN IT IS PRODUCED; `published` is whether it reaches the release page TODAY.
release  the howland-v1.0.0 release page on howland-releases.
artifact an Actions artifact and NEVER the page, by design -- the unsigned twin. Legs build
regardless of certificates and upload under an `unsigned-` artifact name the
release job's take() excludes BY PATH (owner ruling 2026-08-31: building and
publishing are different acts and only the second is gated).
store    App Store Connect, never a release page and never an Actions-artifact substitute.
The iOS .ipa is `published: false` for a CATEGORICALLY DIFFERENT REASON than an unsigned
desktop leg: the leg is waiting for a certificate, the .ipa is refused the page by policy
forever. Collapsed into one state, someone eventually 'fixes' the .ipa onto the page.
THE UNSIGNED DESKTOP TWINS ARE NOT SEPARATE ROWS. They carry IDENTICAL filenames to their
signed selves and are separated by artifact PATH, not by name -- so a row per twin would be
twelve duplicate names declaring nothing. Android is the exception and has its own row:
Howland-Client-Android-debug.apk is a different file, because an unsigned RELEASE apk installs
on no device and a debug-signed one does.
THE MIRROR THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. ../howland/installer/release_assets_test.go carries
desktopReleaseAssets -- a hand-kept 17-name copy of the list below, with 'UPDATE THIS LIST IN
THE SAME CHANGE', in the same file that rules a declaration nothing enforces goes stale. CI
cannot read a sibling repo, so neither side can parse the other. It is named here so the next
reader finds the mirror instead of discovering it. Its TestPublishedAssetTrainIsComplete
asserts 26 = 17 desktop + 9 server, so ANY name added to the train below reddens howland's
count test -- which makes that count an indirect cross-repo tripwire, and it is the only one
there is.

assets.name: Howland-Desktop-macOS-arm64.dmg
assets.why: unsigned, not notarized: no APPLE_DESKTOP_CERT_P12_BASE64 / APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_P8. Builds every run and uploads as unsigned-<leg>; reaches the page the day the certificate lands.

assets.name: Howland-Desktop-macOS-arm64.zip
assets.why: the update payload for latest-mac.yml, gated by the same certificate as its .dmg.

assets.name: Howland-Desktop-macOS-x64.dmg
assets.why: unsigned, not notarized: no APPLE_DESKTOP_CERT_P12_BASE64 / APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_P8. Builds every run and uploads as unsigned-<leg>.

assets.name: Howland-Desktop-macOS-x64.zip
assets.why: the update payload for latest-mac-x64.yml, gated by the same certificate as its .dmg.

assets.name: latest-mac.yml
assets.why: the updater feed rides with the payload it names; an unsigned leg's feed is excluded by artifact path with the binaries it describes.

assets.name: Howland-Desktop-Windows-x64.exe
assets.why: unsigned: no WINDOWS_CERT_PFX_BASE64. Builds every run and uploads as unsigned-<leg>; SmartScreen warns on reputation, which an unsigned binary can never accrue.

assets.name: Howland-Desktop-Windows-arm64.exe
assets.why: unsigned: no WINDOWS_CERT_PFX_BASE64. Builds every run and uploads as unsigned-<leg>.

assets.name: Howland-Client-Android.apk
assets.why: no ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 / ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS / ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD / ANDROID_STORE_PASSWORD. Sideload is a real channel for an offline-first product, so this publishes the day the keystore lands. THIS ONE FILE IS ALSO THE AMAZON APPSTORE ARTIFACT -- Amazon accepts a standard APK, so a second Amazon-named asset would declare a different name for identical bytes. magpie states the same thing at release.yml:273, 'AAB (Play) + APK (Amazon + sideload)', and the uniformity law is the reason to say it the same way rather than invent a flavour here.

assets.name: Howland-Client-Android.aab
assets.why: the Play store-submission artifact; gated by the same keystore as the .apk.

assets.name: Howland-Client-CHECKSUMS.txt
assets.why: the checksum manifest rides with the binaries it describes: if they do not publish, neither does it, for the same reason.

assets.name: Howland-Client-Android-debug.apk
assets.why: NEVER a release asset, by design. It is the unsigned twin, debug-signed because that is the only unsigned form a device will install -- an unsigned release APK is an artifact in name only. Uploads as unsigned-android, which the release job's take() excludes by path. It is how the owner tests before any certificate exists.

assets.name: Howland-Client-iOS-arm64.ipa
assets.why: NEVER a release asset, by policy, not for want of a certificate. App Store Connect is its channel; an .ipa on a public download page installs for nobody and is exposure with no upside. It is a 90-day Actions artifact behind authentication, which is the private hand-off the upload needs.

assets.name: Howland-Desktop-Windows-x64.appx
assets.why: Windows Store package. Built on the existing windows-latest leg and collected as an Actions artifact ONLY — never the release page, until a Partner Center identity exists. appx builds without identityName/publisher/applicationId: those are needed to SUBMIT, not to package.
